name: Grenada
summary_text: Grenada demands real caution. The buggery law (10 years) remains on the books (no successful court challenge yet), though unenforced; no LGR; small community; tourist areas insulated.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust page documents Eastern Caribbean constitutional challenges to criminalising laws; Grenada retains colonial-era buggery provisions.

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda: High Court Decriminalizes Gay Sex | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This HRW article is about Antigua and Barbuda's 2022 ruling, not Grenada specifically; included as Eastern Caribbean regional context.

The Advocates for Human Rights + Khaleem Ali + GrenCHAP UPR stakeholder report (Oct 2024) on LGBTIQ+ rights in Grenada: GrenCHAP has served marginalised groups (LGBT+, PLHIV, sex workers, vulnerable youth) for over 15 years; documents the legal and social situation for the UN review.
The Advocates for Human Rights international submissions index page for Grenada - navigation/landing page linking to their UN advocacy submissions on Grenada.

sources.title: Grenada | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview for Grenada (updated March 2026): same-sex conduct criminalised under Sections 430 ('grossly indecent act') and 431 ('unnatural crime'); no legal gender recognition; no anti-discrimination protections; LGBTIQ people face discrimination in housing, education, employment and public services, harassment and violence; fear of prosecution inhibits reporting to police.

US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for Grenada: significant human-rights issues include laws criminalising consensual sexual conduct between men, though not enforced; otherwise no arbitrary killings, torture or disappearances reported.
